addressPolicyVantageAmbiguity.name: ADDRESS_POLICY_REFUSAL_CAUSED_BY_THE_OPERATOR_VANTAGE
theFacts: all three BLOCKED_BY_POLICY observations this window produced carry resolved_ip_family IPV6 and resolved_ip_is_public false, with no HTTP status
the whole database holds exactly six such rows, all IPv6 and all non-public, in two clusters on this same machine on 2026-09-25: three at about 14:5x UTC and three at about 21:5x UTC

the acquisition vantage is an IPv6-only cellular uplink running DNS64 and NAT64. ipv4only.arpa resolves to 64:ff9b::c000:aa and 64:ff9b::c000:ab, the active interface is marked constrained and carries a CLAT46 address and the well-known CLAT address 192.0.0.2
src/orgunits/web/address.ts classifies 64:ff9b::/96 as relay_or_translation and therefore non-public, and the gateway refuses the whole host when every resolved address is forbidden
under DNS64 an IPv4-only host resolves ONLY into that prefix
addressPolicyVantageAmbiguity.theInference: from this vantage an institution served only over IPv4 is structurally unreachable, and one with native IPv6 is not. R:29:15 returned 31 pages from the same build, the same policy and the same minute
whatIsNOTClaimed: that any of these institutions is unreachable from a dual-stack vantage
that any of them is reachable from one
that the address policy is defective - refusing a translation prefix is the gateway behaving as designed, and rule 18 forbids weakening it
that any earlier adjudication was wrong
addressPolicyVantageAmbiguity.whyTheObligationsAreHELD: the mechanical Q3 derivation for both items is rank 4, MIN_PAGES_NOT_MET, and it is stated in full above so the owner can simply confirm it. What is held is the CONSEQUENCE: creating those obligations leads the next window to spend reserves 19 and 20 against a condition that would refuse ANY IPv4-only host from here. The frozen reserve is finite - 21 of 40 remain - and a reserve spent is never returned. A refusal caused by the operator's uplink is not evidence about the institution, which is the standard this corpus exists to hold
addressPolicyVantageAmbiguity.whyThisIsNewRatherThanAlreadyResolved: the address-policy capability review resolution answered which Q3 RANK an address-policy refusal maps to. It did not have the vantage evidence and did not consider whether such a refusal should create an obligation at all. This is a different question about the same mechanism
addressPolicyVantageAmbiguity.precedentForHolding: slots 51 and 54 were themselves held at PENDING_CAPABILITY_REVIEW after their original refusals, until an owner resolution created their obligations. The same shape is used here
theOwnerOptions: A - confirm the mechanical path: create both obligations at rank 4 and serve them from the next window, accepting that reserves may be spent against the vantage
B - hold both slots until acquisition can run from a dual-stack vantage, and create no obligation now

C - treat an address-policy refusal on a translation prefix as a NON-EVIDENCE outcome that returns the slot to its prior state without consuming the reserve - which would require a governance decision about reserves 16 and 17, already spent
D - something else entirely. This record proposes nothing and decides nothing
